name: Thrush Nightingale
rangeDescription: Northern eurasia; winters to eastern and southern africa
description: Very similar to Common Nightingale, but more dusky brown (not reddish-brown), with a duller and darker rufous tail and a mottled brown (not plain and sandy) breast. Their songs can be confusingly similar, but Thrush Nightingale is more monotonous, less varied, and slower, resembling that of Song Thrush.

name: Buff-throated Warbling Finch
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (southwestern minas gerais and espírito santo to northern são paulo)
description: Medium-sized gray and orange finch from montane forests, including Araucaria forests. Note the black and pale eyebrow.

name: Sichuan Jay
rangeDescription: Mountains of western china (southeastern qinghai, southwestern gansu, and northern sichuan)
description: Sooty jay with a dark head and a bright yellow bill. Unlike many other jays, tends to be quiet and unobtrusive.

name: White-tailed Lapwing
rangeDescription: Southeastern türkiye to afghanistan; winters northeastern africa to india
description: An elegant, rather small lapwing. Pale sandy-brown overall with long, bright yellow legs.

name: Tepui Tinamou
rangeDescription: Tepuis of southern venezuela (ptari-tepui and sororopán-tepui)
description: Unbarred, dark rufous tinamou with a gray face, throat, and belly. With a good view note the pale eyes and orange base to the bill.

name: Chatham Islands Oystercatcher
rangeDescription: Chatham islands (chatham, mangere, rangatira, and pitt)
description: Stocky wader with distinctive pied plumage, red eye surrounded by orange eye-ring, orange bill, and pink legs and feet in adults. Juvenile birds have paler skin and dark tip to bill.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Taiwan Vivid Niltava
rangeDescription: Taiwan
description: Sturdy flycatcher of dense forests, the only regularly occurring niltava on Taiwan. Male distinguished from other blue-and-orange niltavas by orange lower throat and peaked crown.

name: Moseley's Rockhopper Penguin
rangeDescription: Tristan da cunha, gough, st. paul, and amsterdam islands
description: A small black-and-white penguin with a wild, bushy yellow crest. Marine and variably pelagic, foraging offshore and nesting on boulder-strewn beaches and among stands of tussock grass.

name: Moreau's Sunbird
rangeDescription: Mountains of eastern tanzania (nguru, ukaguru, uvidunda, and udzungwa)
description: A medium-sized sunbird. Males are very colorful, with a shining coppery-green iridescence on the head and back and a purple-and-red breast band with yellow sides.

name: Pemba Green-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Pemba (off northeastern tanzania)
description: A medium-sized, chunky pigeon that has an olive-green back and a gray head and underparts. Flight is fast and direct.

name: White-backed Thrush
rangeDescription: Himalayas of western china (gansu to sichuan); winters to northern india
description: Large, boldly-marked thrush of high-altitude open meadows, steppelands, and gardens in central China. Male is dashingly colored with an ivory-white back and breast, a brick-orange belly, and jet-black wings and head.

name: Orange-banded Flycatcher
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of southern ecuador to far northern peru (piura)
description: A small flycatcher restricted to high-elevation Andean cloud forest in southeastern Ecuador and adjacent areas of northern Peru. Darker than other small flycatchers in range and rather distinctive; orange-tinged underparts, buffy wingbars, and mostly orange bill are helpful identification features.

name: Sulphur-throated Finch
rangeDescription: Arid littoral of southwestern ecuador and northwestern peru
description: Drab and nomadic finch-like bird found in desert and arid scrub in northwestern Peru and southwestern Ecuador. While some birds show a distinct yellowish wash on their face and throat and a short mustache, many individuals lack these features, and easily could be confused with female Parrot-billed Seedeater.

name: Yellow-rumped Siskin
rangeDescription: Andes of central peru to northwestern argentina and northern chile
description: Fairly common locally in the Andes, often near bogs or other areas with water. Often in flocks, feeding on the ground or in low bushes.

name: Silver-rumped Spinetail
rangeDescription: Southern myanmar to malay peninsula and greater sundas and satellite islands
description: Small, bullet-shaped swift with rather broad-based wings. Dark (glossy blue in optimal light) with extensive silvery rump patch.

name: Rennell Gerygone
rangeDescription: Rennell (southeastern solomon islands)
description: Small warbler-like bird, endemic to Rennell Island, in the southern Solomon Islands. Fairly distinctive within its tiny range; note the slender black bill, gray cap, white throat, olive back, and yellow belly.

name: Bahama Oriole
rangeDescription: Andros (bahamas); formerly also great and little abaco, where extirpated in 1990s
description: A sleek inhabitant of wooded areas that will venture into gardens and parks in search of flowers and fruit; prefers areas with palms. The adult is distinctive with a black back, head, and chest contrasting with a bright yellow to yellow-orange belly, rump, and shoulders.

name: White-winged Tern
rangeDescription: Palearctic; winters to africa, southern asia, and australasia
description: Buoyant “river tern” with dramatically different breeding and non-breeding plumages. Breeding adult is wildly conspicuous in flight, with contrasting black-and-white plumage; at rest note white shoulders contrasting with black body.

name: Gray-headed Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Northern australia (pilbara, western australia to northwestern and central queensland)
description: Medium-sized honeyeater found in woodlands and rocky areas across northern inland Australia. Olive brown above, yellow with diffuse gray streaking below, with gray crown and dark gray cheek patch bordered in yellow, and entirely black bill during breeding season.

name: Bornean Crestless Fireback
rangeDescription: Lowland forest of northern borneo
description: A rare, compact pheasant of damp tropical lowland rainforest, especially peat swamp forest. Dark overall with bright red facial skin and a cocked, vertically-flattened tail.
